cves.summary: X-AnyLabeling's model downloader disabled TLS certificate verification. download_with_retry in anylabeling/services/auto_labeling/model.py built a context with ssl._create_unverified_context() and passed it to urllib.req
cves.headline: X-AnyLabeling before 4.0.0-beta.9 downloads models without checking TLS certificates

name: Improper Certificate Validation
title: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation
ai_text: In AI software this weakness shows up in tools that pull models or data from the network. The one CVE here is in X-AnyLabeling, an annotation tool built on PyTorch, which downloads models without checking TLS certificates. The flaw is reached when the tool fetches a model over a connection it never verifies, so a party in the middle can stand in for the real source. What that lets an attacker do is feed the tool a model or file of their choosing, which the user then loads and runs as if it came from the expected place. The result is untrusted content entering a machine that trusts it.
description: The product does not validate, or incorrectly validates, a certificate.

mitigations.description: Certificates should be carefully managed and checked to assure that data are encrypted with the intended owner's public key.
If certificate pinning is being used, ensure that all relevant properties of the certificate are fully validated before the certificate is pinned, including the hostname.

consequences.note: When a certificate is invalid or malicious, it might allow an attacker to spoof a trusted entity by interfering in the communication path between the host and client. The product might connect to a malicious host while believing it is a trusted host, or the product might be deceived into accepting spoofed data that appears to originate from a trusted host.
